title: Smooth-stratum finite-Tor devissage over an arbitrary algebraically closed field
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field, $A$ a finite commutative ring, and $X$ a separated finite-type $F$-scheme. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on small etale sites and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $a\leq b$ be integers and let $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ be bounded constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, meaning that $\mathcal H^q(K\otimes_A^LM)=0$ for every module sheaf $M$ in degree zero and every $q\notin[a,b]$ [def-kun-derived-tensor, def-kun-tor-amplitude].

There is a finite partition of the underlying space of $X$ into reduced (with no nonzero nilpotents in their local rings), smooth, connected (not a union of two disjoint nonempty open subsets) locally closed $F$-subschemes $s_r:S_r\hookrightarrow X$, each of pure dimension $e_r\leq\dim X$, meaning that every irreducible component has dimension $e_r$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with the following properties. Put $P_r=s_r^{-1}K$ using exact constant-coefficient inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Each $P_r$ has finite locally constant cohomology. There is an etale cover of $S_r$ on which $P_r$ is represented by a complex of constant finite projective $A$-modules zero outside $[a,b]$; a finite projective $A$-module here means a direct summand of a finite free $A$-module.

Moreover there are objects $F_0=K,F_1,\ldots,F_m=0$ and distinguished triangles
$$Rs_{r!}P_r\longrightarrow F_{r-1}\longrightarrow F_r\longrightarrow Rs_{r!}P_r[1]\qquad(1\leq r\leq m).$$
Here $Rs_{r!}=j_!i_*$ for a factorization $S_r\xrightarrow{i}V\xrightarrow{j}X$ with $i$ closed and $j$ open; the closed direct image is exact, and $j_!$ is ordinary etale extension by zero [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement, def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. The triangles are in the ordinary etale derived category [def-weil-triangulated-category]. No restriction of $F$ to an algebraic closure of a finite field is imposed.

proof.text: A finite ring $A$ is Noetherian: any ideal is a finite set and is generated by that set. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the whole field. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian, and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] gives finite dimension. Taking the degree-zero sheaf $M=A_X$ in [def-kun-tor-amplitude] gives $\mathcal H^qK=0$ outside $[a,b]$, since $K\otimes_A^L A_X=K$: in the definition [def-kun-derived-tensor], take a K-flat representative $B^\bullet$ of $K$ and use the degreewise isomorphisms $B^q\otimes_{A_X}A_X\to B^q$, $z\otimes c\mapsto cz$, which commute with differentials. Exact constant-coefficient inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] commutes with cohomology: it preserves the kernel and image defining each cohomology sheaf. Constructibility of these cohomology sheaves is preserved by any restriction to a subscheme by [prop-constructible-pullback].

source.place: Tag 03TT (lemma-when-ctf), hypotheses; finite type over a field: morphisms.tex Tag 01T6; restriction and the unit tensor identity are agent explanations.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] with the closed subset $|X|$ to form $h:T_0=X_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow X$. Put $L_0=h^{-1}K$. The complementary open is empty, whose category of module sheaves has only the zero object (the sheaf condition for the empty covering forces this). The triangle of [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] therefore gives $K\xrightarrow{\sim}h_*L_0$: its first term is zero. Equivalently, the short exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] with empty complement gives this isomorphism degreewise. We can work on the reduced $T_0$ and then push the eventual tower to $X$. In particular this step does not pretend that a nonreduced $X$ itself has a smooth dense open.

Every closed subset $Z\subseteq |T_0|$ has the reduced induced closed subscheme $T=Z_{\mathrm{red}}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; write $k:T\hookrightarrow X$ for its inclusion. It is finite type over $F$: on an affine chart of $X$ its algebra is a quotient of a finitely generated $F$-algebra, generated by the images of the original generators. Its underlying closed subset is quasi-compact, so finitely many such charts suffice. Hence $T$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Every open of $T$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] and remains finite type over $F$: choose finitely many principal affine charts, whose rings are obtained by adjoining an inverse to the finitely generated chart rings. Its structure morphism is separated by restriction of that of $X$. For $L=k^{-1}K$, step 1 gives bounded constructible cohomology. Apply [prop-constructible-generic-constancy] to each of the finitely many possibly nonzero sheaves $\mathcal H^qL$ and intersect the resulting dense opens. This gives a dense open $W\subseteq T$ where all cohomology sheaves of $L$ are finite locally constant. A finite intersection of dense opens is dense: successively intersect any nonempty open with each dense open.

source.place: Agent finite simultaneous refinement of constructibility; blueprint prop-constructible-generic-constancy; schemes.tex Tag 01J3; properties.tex Tags 01OW, 01OZ.

proof.text:
The algebraically closed field $F$ is perfect: in positive characteristic $p$, every element has a root of $t^p-c$, so Frobenius is surjective; in characteristic zero perfection is automatic. Since $T$ is reduced and finite type, [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect] says it is geometrically reduced and its structure morphism is finitely presented. Thus [lem-pur-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open] gives a dense smooth open $W_{\mathrm{sm}}\subseteq T$. There are finitely many irreducible components $C_1,\ldots,C_t$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]. For nonempty $T$ put
$$U_i=(W\cap W_{\mathrm{sm}})\cap\bigl(T\setminus\textstyle\bigcup_{j\ne i}C_j\bigr).$$
Each $U_i$ is a nonempty open of $T$, lies in $C_i$, and is irreducible: a nonempty open of an irreducible space is irreducible, and a dense open of $T$ meets the nonempty open $T\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}C_j$. The $U_i$ are pairwise disjoint. Their union is dense, because its complement is the union of $T\setminus(W\cap W_{\mathrm{sm}})$ and the finitely many component intersections; an intersection $C_i\cap C_j$ contains no component, so has empty interior. Each $U_i$ is reduced, smooth over $F$, connected, and has finite locally constant cohomology of $L$. Irreducibility implies connectedness directly: two disjoint nonempty opens covering it contradict the definition of irreducibility.

proof.text:
The construction terminates with finitely many strata. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] permits induction on closed subsets of $T_0$. The induction assertion is that a reduced induced closed subscheme has a finite ordered decomposition obtained by repeatedly removing a smooth irreducible open with lisse cohomology. The empty subset has the empty decomposition. For nonempty $T$ take the finite disjoint family $U_i$ of step 4; the complement of their dense union is a strictly smaller closed subset. Give it the reduced induced structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] and apply the induction assertion. Remove the $U_i$ one at a time first, then follow that complementary decomposition. After removing earlier $U_i$, a later $U_j$ is still an open subscheme of the remaining reduced closed subscheme, with its original scheme structure: on $U_j$ the reduced induced closed subscheme has full support and, by uniqueness in the cited reduced-induced statement, equals $U_j$. We obtain closed immersions
$$T_m=\varnothing\hookrightarrow T_{m-1}\hookrightarrow\cdots\hookrightarrow T_0$$
with $S_r=T_{r-1}\setminus T_r$ smooth, reduced and irreducible; denote $u_r:S_r\hookrightarrow T_{r-1}$ and $k_r:T_r\hookrightarrow X$. These subsets partition $|X|$. Set $e_r=\dim S_r$. There is only one irreducible component of $S_r$, so it is pure of dimension $e_r$. To check $e_r\leq\dim X$ using [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], close any strict chain of irreducible relatively closed subsets of $S_r$ in $X$. The closures are irreducible and remain distinct since their intersections with $S_r$ recover the original subsets. Thus the chain length is bounded by $\dim X$. In particular every $e_r$ is finite by step 1.

proof.text: For every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ the ring complex $K_{\bar x}$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$. For an arbitrary $A$-module $N$ take its constant module sheaf $N_X$. The hypothesis says $\mathcal H^q(K\otimes_A^L N_X)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. Exact stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], their identification with geometric inverse image [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback], and the derived tensor/pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identify its stalk with $H^q(K_{\bar x}\otimes_A^L N)$. Here $(N_X)_{\bar x}=N$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk]; the same identification for $A$ identifies the coefficient ring with $A$. All maps are $A$-linear by the inverse-image module structure in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Hence this vanishes for every $N$ and every $q\notin[a,b]$. This checks the ring-theoretic Tor condition, including infinite $A$-modules, rather than assuming it from boundedness alone.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), at a geometric point; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact). Agent stalkwise Tor test used in the proof of Tag 09BI.

proof.text: Put $s_r=k_{r-1}u_r:S_r\hookrightarrow X$ and $P_r=s_r^{-1}K$. The inverse-image composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] and exact inverse image identify the cohomology of $P_r$ with the restrictions already shown lisse in steps 3--5. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-derived-local-constancy] on $S_r$, with the same finite ring $A$; it supplies an etale cover on which $P_r$ is isomorphic to the constant complex associated to a bounded complex $E^\bullet$ of finite $A$-modules. Discard empty members and choose a geometric point on each remaining member.

proof.text: For a cover member $t:U\to S_r$ and its chosen geometric point $\bar u$, apply [lem-sf-etale-stratified-stalk-identification] to the composite $f=s_rt$ and the isomorphism $f^{-1}K\simeq\underline{E^\bullet}_U$ from step 7. It gives $E^\bullet\simeq K_{f\bar u}$ in $D(A)$, as complexes over the same ring $A$. Step 6 therefore gives $E^\bullet$ Tor amplitude $[a,b]$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-bounded-finite-tor-perfect] to obtain a complex $Q^\bullet$ of finite projective $A$-modules, zero outside $[a,b]$, isomorphic to $E^\bullet$ in $D(A)$. By [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], each term is a direct summand of a finite free module: choose finitely many generators and split the resulting finite-free surjection. By [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative], the derived isomorphism is represented by an actual cochain map $Q^\bullet\to E^\bullet$, which is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09BI (lemma-connected-ctf-locally-constant), proof via sites-cohomology.tex Tag 094G (lemma-locally-constant), with the prescribed interval from more-algebra.tex Tag 0658 (lemma-perfect); constant exactness Tag 03RX. Agent chain-map explanation.

proof.text: The cone $C^\bullet$ of the quasi-isomorphism in step 9 is bounded, finite termwise, and acyclic. The constant module functor is additive and exact by [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $H^q(\underline{C^\bullet})\cong\underline{H^q(C^\bullet)}=0$. Since an additive functor commutes with the finite direct sums and signed differential defining a cone, $\underline{C^\bullet}$ is the cone of $\underline{Q^\bullet}\to\underline{E^\bullet}$. This map is a quasi-isomorphism, yielding the required local constant finite-projective model in the original interval $[a,b]$.

proof.text:
Write $v_r:T_r\hookrightarrow T_{r-1}$ for the complementary closed immersion and $L_{r-1}=k_{r-1}^{-1}K$. The bounded-below localization statement [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] gives
$$u_{r!}u_r^{-1}L_{r-1}\longrightarrow L_{r-1}\longrightarrow v_{r*}v_r^{-1}L_{r-1}\longrightarrow u_{r!}u_r^{-1}L_{r-1}[1].$$
Push this triangle to $X$ by $k_{r-1,*}$. Its exactness for a closed immersion is part of the cited recollement statement, and [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] says explicitly that the induced termwise functor preserves distinguished triangles. By the direct- and inverse-image composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] the middle and third terms are $k_{r-1,*}k_{r-1}^{-1}K$ and $k_{r*}k_r^{-1}K$. The first restriction is $P_r$. Define $F_r=k_{r*}k_r^{-1}K$ for $1\leq r\leq m$ and use $F_0=K$, transporting the first triangle along the isomorphism of step 2. The last term $F_m$ is zero since $T_m$ is empty. It remains to identify the first term of each triangle with the prescribed $Rs_{r!}P_r$.

proof.text:
Let $V_r=X\setminus |k_r(T_r)|$ with open inclusion $j_r:V_r\hookrightarrow X$. The intersection $T_{r-1}\times_XV_r$ is exactly the open subscheme $S_r$ of $T_{r-1}$: this is an actual base change, not factorization based only on containment of images. Thus the other map $i_r:S_r\hookrightarrow V_r$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], and $s_r=j_ri_r$. The morphism $k_{r-1}$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]; $j_r$ is quasi-compact: for every affine open $B\subseteq X$, its inverse image is $B\cap V_r$, an open subscheme of the Noetherian $X$, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-open-proper-interchange] to this cartesian square and $P_r\in D^+(S_r{}_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. It gives
$$k_{r-1,*}u_{r!}P_r\cong j_{r!}i_{r*}P_r.$$
Both proper direct images here are already exact closed direct images by [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement], so they agree with their derived functors. By [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] the open functor is ordinary etale extension by zero. The right side is precisely the $Rs_{r!}P_r$ specified in the statement. Substitute this isomorphism in the triangles of step 11 to get every required triangle. All constructions used the actual algebraically closed field $F$ and finite constant ring $A$; no characteristic restriction or finite-field-origin restriction was used.
